First supported population refusal stops event evaluation. The retained complete A/B/C observations remain the evidence for other transitions; the event list is not claimed exhaustive after refusal. No native admission follows a refusal.

Current driver streams may be written after the final accounting observation. Existing accounting_boundary remains explicit; this point-in-time check is not final dataset intake or a filesystem quota. No complete-final-byte or reuse claim is made.

Actual stdout/stderr file descriptors are checked with fstat and same-file identity against lineage-bound paths before reservation, in binding/accounting checks, at refusal retention and before final output. Prior preparation stderr must be empty; nonempty bytes refuse.
Secondary terminal reasons and *_error fields refuse historical intake; original primary preclaim error remains valid evidence of refusal.
Campaign basename and serialized binding spelling remain exact. Case or spelling variants may refuse; paths are not silently normalized into wider acceptance.
